title: Information Security Access Policy
text: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for remote access, cloud applications, administrator consoles, and systems containing confidential or restricted data. Employees must use an approved authenticator application or hardware security key; SMS is permitted only as a documented temporary recovery method.

title: Information Security Access Policy
text: Passwords must contain at least fourteen characters and must not reuse any of the previous twelve passwords. Password managers are required for service-specific credentials. Suspected exposure requires an immediate reset and notification to the security operations team.

title: Information Security Access Policy
text: Privileged administrator access must use a separate named account, just-in-time elevation, and a maximum approval window of eight hours. Shared administrator accounts are prohibited. Every privileged session is logged and reviewed by Information Security each month.

title: Information Security Access Policy
text: Managers and system owners must complete quarterly access certifications for confidential and restricted systems. Unneeded access must be removed within two business days, and overdue reviews are escalated to the responsible vice president after five business days.

title: Information Security Access Policy
text: Remote connections to internal resources must use the company VPN from a managed device with current endpoint protection and disk encryption. Split tunneling is disabled for restricted environments, and users must report lost devices to the service desk within one hour.

title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Playbook
text: Security incidents are classified from Severity 1 through Severity 4. Severity 1 covers active compromise with material business impact and requires fifteen-minute escalation; Severity 2 requires one-hour escalation, while lower severities follow the standard service workflow.

title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Playbook
text: Employees must report suspected phishing, malware, unauthorized access, or data exposure immediately through the security hotline or incident portal. The report should include the affected device, observed time, screenshots when safe, and any actions already taken.

title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Playbook
text: The incident commander selects short-term containment actions based on business risk. Approved actions include isolating endpoints, disabling compromised identities, blocking indicators, and segmenting networks. Destructive remediation must wait until volatile evidence has been preserved.

title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Playbook
text: Responders must preserve logs, memory captures, disk images, and relevant communications using documented chain-of-custody records. Evidence receives a unique identifier, collection timestamp, collector name, SHA-256 checksum, and access history before legal review.

title: Cybersecurity Incident Response Playbook
text: Only the designated communications lead may release incident statements to customers, regulators, or the media. Legal approves notification content and timing, while the incident commander supplies confirmed facts. Team members must not speculate through personal channels.

title: Enterprise Data Governance Standard
text: Information owners classify data as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted. Classification determines encryption, sharing, storage, and disposal controls. Restricted data includes regulated personal information, authentication secrets, and unreleased financial records.

title: Enterprise Data Governance Standard
text: Data stewards apply the approved retention schedule and document any litigation hold before disposal. When a retention period expires, records must be securely deleted from active systems and scheduled backup cycles, with disposal evidence retained for three years.

title: Enterprise Data Governance Standard
text: Critical data elements require documented owners, validation rules, and quality thresholds for completeness, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness. Pipelines must quarantine failed records, publish quality results, and alert the accountable steward when a threshold is breached.

title: Enterprise Data Governance Standard
text: External sharing of Confidential or Restricted data requires a recorded business purpose, owner approval, legal review, and a data-processing agreement. Only the minimum necessary fields may be transferred through an approved encrypted channel.

title: Travel and Expense Policy
text: Employees must book air, hotel, and rail travel through the approved corporate travel portal. Economy class is required for flights under six hours. A manager must approve exceptions before purchase, and personal loyalty preferences cannot increase company cost.

title: Travel and Expense Policy
text: Business travel meals are reimbursed up to seventy-five dollars per traveler per day, including tax and gratuity. Alcohol is not reimbursable unless it is part of a preapproved client event. Attendee names and business purpose are required for group meals.

title: Travel and Expense Policy
text: An itemized receipt is required for every expense of twenty-five dollars or more. If a receipt is unavailable, the employee must submit a missing-receipt declaration with the amount, date, vendor, and manager approval before reimbursement can proceed.

title: Travel and Expense Policy
text: Expense reports must be submitted within ten calendar days after travel and approved by the employee's manager. Finance processes complete, policy-compliant reports within seven business days. Personal, duplicate, and unsupported expenses are rejected.

title: Third-Party Vendor Management Standard
text: Before onboarding a vendor that handles company data, Procurement must complete financial and operational due diligence while Security assesses controls, breach history, data location, and subcontractors. High-risk findings require a documented remediation plan and owner acceptance.

title: Third-Party Vendor Management Standard
text: Vendor contracts must include confidentiality, breach notification within twenty-four hours, audit rights, data return or deletion, subcontractor obligations, minimum cyber insurance of five million dollars, and liability language approved by Legal.

title: Third-Party Vendor Management Standard
text: Critical vendors are reassessed annually and monitored for security ratings, service availability, ownership changes, and reported incidents. Material control deterioration creates a corrective action ticket with a due date and accountable vendor owner.

title: Third-Party Vendor Management Standard
text: At contract termination, the vendor owner coordinates account revocation, integration shutdown, asset recovery, and data return or certified deletion. Procurement records completion evidence, and Security validates removal of network and application access.

title: Business Continuity and Recovery Plan
text: Each critical service must maintain an approved recovery time objective and recovery point objective. Tier 1 services target a four-hour RTO and one-hour RPO; owners must document dependencies and obtain executive approval for any unmet objective.

title: Business Continuity and Recovery Plan
text: Tier 1 production data is backed up daily with encrypted copies stored in a separate recovery environment. Infrastructure performs quarterly restoration tests, records recovery duration and integrity checks, and remediates failures within ten business days.

title: Business Continuity and Recovery Plan
text: Business units participate in one tabletop continuity exercise each year, and critical technology teams conduct a technical recovery exercise at least annually. Exercise reports identify decisions, actual recovery times, gaps, owners, and corrective-action deadlines.

title: Business Continuity and Recovery Plan
text: Employees should use the emergency notification system for building closures and continuity instructions. Managers verify team contact details every quarter. During an outage, staff must follow the published call tree and acknowledge safety messages promptly.
